Resolves #19773

🌿 *Scene 2 can no longer fail on its own instruments, or drive a hand no user has, before it gets home.*

Scene 2 (native titlebar) is the native-return witness #16498's discharge depends on. It had not reached its return since 09-02, because test-side gates drifted under product changes that no CI tier runs it against. This PR lines the scene up with the contracts it reads:
- The stage parity compares the frame with `outerRect`, because since #18068 the manager publishes `innerRect` at the viewport origin.
- The `swift -e` compile now happens before the 15 s witnesses open.
- The return is validated as the `transferItem` out of the vessel that #18677 made it.
- The hand brings the popup's **corner** anchor onto the target, as it has been since #18059, instead of the popup's centre.
- The hand now watches its corner. The window server resists a popup whose edge meets main's edge; a plain Chrome popup shows the same 94 px x-loss with no Neo code involved. Before the gesture, `identifyNativeWindow` binds the sensor to the one window whose frame is the popup's known frame, and fails loud on none or several. The swift hand then reads only that window number, keeps dragging until the corner lands, and reports the landing or a lost sensor.

Evidence: L3 (headed runs on the operator's display: real Chrome, literal HID input) → L3 required (AC 1–4; CI never runs this scene). Residual: AC 4's end-to-end pass, Residual-Owner: #19775 (its fix, #19779, removes the last red).

| AC-4 | outside-CI: the return is reached and committed exactly as predicted at this head. With the bound sensor the corner lands on target (`sensorLost: false`, `corrections: 1`, landed within 0.25 px). The end-to-end pass needs #19779's fix: green at the combined head, 11.5 s |

## Deltas from ticket

- Gates 4a/4b were found by the operator watching the runs: first the centre-aimed corner landed outside the body, then the arrows appeared away from the corner. The 4b cause was isolated with a plain Chrome popup: an opener under the path absorbs 94 px of x, and with no window under the path the drag is exact.
- `readBrowserSurface` still names the frame origin `inner.x/y`. Its other consumers compare it with frame values (`filmStage.mjs:118`, `:206`, `:445`) and stay correct, so a rename is out of scope.

## Test Evidence

Headed runs of `scene 2 (native titlebar)` on the operator's display, each after one changed variable; #19773's Context table has the per-run receipts. The `#16756` place-cycle arm also passed; its receipt is on #16498. CI skips this scene, since it needs darwin plus `NEO_FILM_TAKE=1` plus `--headed`. The sensor binder's negative controls run in CI: `test/playwright/unit/e2e/filmStage.spec.mjs` › "identifyNativeWindow binds the sensor to the window it will read". They cover a foreign same-size window at the destination, a missing popup, an ambiguous frame and the tolerance edge.

## Addressed Review Feedback

Responding to review [5540161404](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19776#pullrequestreview-5540161404). The finding is right. The selector picked whichever same-size window sat nearest `land`, so a foreign window there, or the popup's absence, read as a perfect landing. That is the very error the loop exists to measure. "Reads the popup frame back" overstated it, and the body now says what the sensor actually reads.

**Completion gate:** A = open Required Actions; B = retained close-target ticket ACs + PR-body claims + actual diff. A is empty relative to B at this head.

- [x] **`[ADDRESSED]`** Bind the native feedback sensor to the intended popup before the drag, retain that native window identity for every corrective read and the final landing receipt, and fail explicitly if it is missing or cannot be identified uniquely. Add negative controls for a same-size foreign window nearer the destination and for disappearance of the intended popup, then refresh the headed landing receipt with the repaired sensor. Keep the gesture as literal HID input.
      **Commit:** `712fc9ce93`
      **Details:**
      - **Bind before the drag.** `identifyNativeWindow` (`test/playwright/e2e/utils/filmStage.mjs`) is a pure binder: it picks exactly one on-screen window whose frame is the popup's *known* frame before the gesture (browser `screenX/Y` + outer size), with 1 px tolerance per edge. It throws on none or several. Scene 2 lists the windows once (`listNativeWindows`), binds the popup's window number, and passes only that number to the hand.
      - **Read only that window.** The swift hand reads `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo([.optionIncludingWindow], popupWindow)` for every correction and for the landing receipt. A missing window ends the corrections and prints `sensorLost`. The scene then asserts `sensorLost: false`, and the ≤2 px landing check fails on the resulting NaN.
      - **Negative controls** run in CI in `test/playwright/unit/e2e/filmStage.spec.mjs`, with your numbers: an intended 800×600 popup at (906,200) and a destination 94 px right.
        - A foreign same-size window at the destination is never bound; the popup is.
        - A missing popup throws, even with the foreign window present.
        - Two windows on the popup's frame are ambiguous and throw.
        - The tolerance edge (1 px binds, 2 px doesn't).
        - 24/24 pass.
      - **Disappearance mid-drag** is the swift `sensorLost` branch, which only runs headed. I didn't reproduce it by closing the popup mid-gesture on the operator's display.
      - **Headed refresh** on #19776's head plus #19779's two commits: scene 2 passes end-to-end (11.5 s) with `sensorLost: false, corrections: 1`, landed at (2946, 358) against a target of (2946, 358.25). The gesture stays literal HID input; the binding is read-only window-server metadata.

All Required Actions are discharged against B at this head.
CI hold: checks for `712fc9ce93` are still running. I'll send the re-review request once they are green.
